overall: The AG found both the Northampton City Council and School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by giving vague executive session topics and purposes in notices and votes; later amendments did not cure this, and the Committee's detrimental-effect statement claim was rejected.

allegations.summary: Council meeting notices (May 5, May 19, June 2, 2011) listed the executive session topic only as collective bargaining strategy, allegedly too vague.
allegations.key_passage: The meeting notices for the Council's May 5, May 19, and June 2, 2011 meetings fell short of the requirement that the Council state "all subjects that may be revealed without compromising the purpose for which the executive session" was being called.

allegations.summary: At the May 5, 2011 Council meeting, the motion to enter executive session gave no reason for the session, allegedly too little detail.
allegations.key_passage: This statement obviously failed to provide enough information so that a member of the public would understand the nature of the executive session.

allegations.summary: The Council chair did not state before the May 5, 2011 executive session that an open discussion could harm the body's bargaining position.
allegations.key_passage: That did not occur prior to the May 5, 2011 executive session, however we are confident that the Council understands its obligations in this regard

allegations.summary: The Council's after-the-fact amendment of agendas and open session minutes was offered as remedy for the notice and entry-statement defects.
allegations.key_passage: we note that the Council's amendment of its meeting agendas and open session minutes was not sufficient to cure the deficiencies in the meeting notice and the statement made at the time the Council entered executive session.

allegations.summary: School Committee's May 26, 2011 notice said only that executive session was to discuss collective bargaining, allegedly too vague.
allegations.key_passage: For the same reasons that the Council's meeting notices were not sufficiently specific, the notice for the Committee's meeting on May 26, 2011 also failed to comply with the law's requirements.

allegations.summary: The School Committee's notice did not tell the public that an open session would be held before the executive session.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee acted appropriately by convening in open session prior to entering executive session, however there was no notice to the public that this open session would occur.

allegations.summary: The School Committee's motion to enter executive session did not name the negotiating group (NASE), allegedly too vague.
allegations.key_passage: this information should have been in the meeting notice and should also have been included in the statement of the executive session purpose at the time the Committee voted to enter executive session.

allegations.summary: The School Committee allegedly failed to state that open discussion would harm its bargaining position before entering executive session.
allegations.key_passage: the executive session minutes indicate that this statement was actually made.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (applies to both the City Council and the School Committee).
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution the Council and the Committee that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
